compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
A live cache canary run under `wayward-taxidermal-nauplius` (`f91e-57a2-f790-4ebd`) measured
that a single-model structured call caches normally on BOTH providers (direct Anthropic and
Bedrock: a ~10.7k-token prefix written to cache on call 1, read back on call 2). The SAME
session's plan-review gate run, on the same Bedrock model, recorded 32 LLM calls,
785,178 input tokens, `cache_read_tokens = 0` and `cache_write_tokens = 0`, with provider
provenance `prompt_cache_style = "none"` over the candidate chain
`["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6", "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"]`.

The zeroing is deliberate, not a defect: `runner_support._intersect_capabilities` collapses
disagreeing `prompt_cache_style` values to `"none"` because each provider's cache keys are
provider-specific and would error on the candidate that does not share them, and `rebar.toml`
records the same fact ("Mixed-provider chains disable prompt caching because their
provider-specific cache keys do not intersect").

The problem is that `docs/llm-framework.md`'s accounting section — the section an operator
reads to reconcile observed cache counts — does not mention it. So an operator who sees a real
gate run report 0/0 while a hand-run single-model call caches fine has no explanation in the
document that is supposed to be the accounting contract, and the natural conclusion is
"caching regressed", which is wrong.

## Approach
Add a short subsection to the accounting section of `docs/llm-framework.md` stating that a
fallback chain's capability record is the conservative intersection over its candidates, that
disagreeing prompt-cache styles therefore collapse to no caching for the whole chain, and that
this is why a chain-backed op can legitimately report `cache_read_tokens = 0` and
`cache_write_tokens = 0` while the same model called alone caches normally. Point at the
authority (`runner_support._intersect_capabilities`) rather than restating its logic, and cross
reference the shipped configuration note in `rebar.toml`, so there is one source of truth and
the doc stays a pointer.

Documentation only, because the runtime behaviour is already the intended one and is already
recorded in code and in the shipped config; the only thing missing is that the operator-facing
accounting section does not carry it.

## Scope
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — add the fallback-chain caching note to the structured retry/
  accounting section.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md`'s structured retry/accounting section states that a
  mixed-provider fallback chain resolves to no prompt caching, and names
  `runner_support._intersect_capabilities` as the authority. Checked by reading the section and
  confirming both the statement and the symbol reference are present.
- [ ] The note explains the observable consequence in the operator's own terms — that an op
  running on such a chain reports zero cache read and zero cache write while the same model
  called on its own caches normally — so a 0/0 reading is not mistaken for a regression.
  Checked by reading the section for that explicit contrast.

file_impact.reason: add a fallback-chain prompt-caching note to the structured retry/accounting section so an operator can reconcile a 0/0 cache reading from a chain-backed op

compiled_state.title: Document that a mixed-provider fallback chain disables prompt caching in the llm-framework accounting section
